plan: Reduce QQQI to 20% to lower concentration.

conservative.read: This plan prioritizes capital preservation. Expect a lower target return of around 1.5% per month. Drawdowns should be minimal, but upside potential is also limited.

Trim AI/Software leveraged ETFs (METU, PLTU) to 3% and 2%.

balanced.read: This balanced approach aims for risk-first growth, targeting around 2.5% per month. It blends stability with calculated risk. Drawdowns are expected to be moderate.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% while maintaining income exposure.
Increase leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU) to 6% each.
Add to leveraged AI/Software ETFs (METU, PLTU, MSFU) to 6% each.
Concentrate exposure in high-conviction, high-scoring scanner setups.

aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets stretched growth, aiming for around 4% per month. It leans heavily into leverage and concentration, significantly increasing potential upside and downside. Be aware of leveraged ETF decay and the potential for large, rapid losses.

plan: Increase QQQI allocation to 30% for higher income potential.
Exit all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU, PLTU, MSFU) to reduce volatility.

income.read: This income-focused plan targets approximately 1% per month through distributions. It prioritizes capital preservation and steady income over growth. While aiming for low drawdowns, the Net Asset Value can still decline in market downturns.
